# Proposed Change

## Change Type(s)
Put an `x` in each box that applies.

- [ ] :sparkles: `(feat)` **New Feature** (non-breaking change to add functionality)
- [ ] :bug: `(fix)`  **Bug Fix** (non-breaking change to fix an issue)
- [ ] :recycle: `(redo)` **Code Refactoring** (low-risk structural changes or rework without changing intended feature scope)
- [ ] :memo: `(docs)` **Documentation Update** (comments, documentation, etc.)
- [ ] :test_tube: `(test)` **Testing Implementation** (unit, integration, smoke, regression, etc.)
- [ ] :broom: `(chore)` **Chore / Maintenance** (maintenance or setup, such as pipelines, gitignore, etc.)
- [ ] :stopwatch: `(perf)` **Performance / Optimization** (performance improvement and benchmarking)
- [ ] :shield: `(vuls)` **Security / Vulnerability** (addressing security issues and vulnerabilities)

## Summary
Describe the change in direct terms. State what changed, why it changed, and what part of the project it affects.

## Linked Issue
Closes or relates to: `#<issue-number>`

## Validation
- [ ] I built the project locally without errors.
- [ ] I ran the relevant tests locally.
- [ ] I ran local formatting and lint checks.
- [ ] I verified this change against the issue acceptance criteria.
- [ ] I updated documentation or comments where needed.
- [ ] Identifier names follow the repository naming rules in `docs/naming.md`.
- [ ] My changes remain compatible with the C++14 target.
- [ ] I updated `CHANGELOG.md` to properly describe pull request changes.
- [ ] My PR title includes a short change description that can be used as the squash merge commit message.
- [ ] My final squash merge commit message follows the mandated format, for example `feat: add CSV parser (Issue #2)`.

## Additional Notes
Include benchmark notes, design decisions, recovery implications, comment-sensitive areas, or any other context that will help a reviewer understand the pull request quickly.
